SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-Workspace-Projects---ai-mcp-mcp-yandex-tracker/8e212f67-5f23-4877-b23d-5393c99f2300/scratchpad
cat > $SP/en_block.md <<'EOF'
The three entity types share one tool set, so it is listed once - the row says what the
tool does, the columns which name to call:

| What it does | Projects | Portfolios | Goals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One entity by id or shortId | `project_get` | `portfolio_get` | `goal_get` |
| Search by name substring and/or field filters; returns `{values, hits, pages}` | `project_find` | `portfolio_find` | `goal_find` |
| A page of comments; returns `{comments, next_cursor}` | `project_get_comments` | `portfolio_get_comments` | `goal_get_comments` |
| Create, returning the entity | `project_create` | `portfolio_create` | `goal_create` |
| Change any field creation takes | `project_update` | `portfolio_update` | `goal_update` |
| Delete it, and with `with_board` its board too | `project_delete` | `portfolio_delete` | `goal_delete` (no `with_board`) |
| Add a comment | `project_add_comment` | `portfolio_add_comment` | `goal_add_comment` |
| Edit a comment | `project_update_comment` | `portfolio_update_comment` | `goal_update_comment` |
| Delete a comment | `project_delete_comment` | `portfolio_delete_comment` | `goal_delete_comment` |
| Append one checklist item | `project_add_checklist_item` | `portfolio_add_checklist_item` | - |
| Edit one checklist item, leaving the fields you omit as they are | `project_update_checklist_item` | `portfolio_update_checklist_item` | - |
| Move a checklist item before another one | `project_move_checklist_item` | `portfolio_move_checklist_item` | - |
| Delete one checklist item | `project_delete_checklist_item` | `portfolio_delete_checklist_item` | - |
| Edit several existing items by id | `project_update_checklist` | `portfolio_update_checklist` | - |
| Delete the whole checklist | `project_delete_checklist` | `portfolio_delete_checklist` | - |

- **Arguments.** Reads take `entity_id` and `fields`; the `*_find` tools take `input`, `filter`, `order_by`, `order_asc`, `root_only`, `page`, `per_page`. Create and update take `summary` (required on create), `description`, `lead`, `team_users`, `clients`, `followers`, `start` (goals have none), `end`, `tags`, `entity_status`, `parent_entity`, `team_access` and `links`, and update also `comment` and `version` (optimistic locking). Every tool takes the same `fields` selector and returns the entity.
- **`links` are added, never replaced**, and the API never returns them: an existing link cannot be read back or removed through this server, and a links-only update is rejected rather than reported as a success Tracker silently ignores.
- **Not in the default field set:** `checklistItems` (the checklist tools return the whole entity, so ask for them to see the result), `metricItems`, and a goal's `keyResultItems` - the last two are read-only. Goals use their own `entityStatus` values (`draft`, `according_to_plan`, `at_risk`, `blocked`, `achieved`, `partially_achieved`, `not_achieved`, `exceeded`, `cancelled`). Bulk changes are not supported.
EOF
cat > $SP/ru_block.md <<'EOF'
Все три типа сущностей используют один и тот же набор инструментов, поэтому он перечислен
один раз: строка говорит, что делает инструмент, а столбцы — как он называется:

| Что делает | Проекты | Портфели | Цели |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Одна сущность по id или shortId | `project_get` | `portfolio_get` | `goal_get` |
| Поиск по подстроке в названии и/или фильтрам полей; возвращает `{values, hits, pages}` | `project_find` | `portfolio_find` | `goal_find` |
| Страница комментариев; возвращает `{comments, next_cursor}` | `project_get_comments` | `portfolio_get_comments` | `goal_get_comments` |
| Создать и вернуть сущность | `project_create` | `portfolio_create` | `goal_create` |
| Изменить любое поле из тех, что принимает создание | `project_update` | `portfolio_update` | `goal_update` |
| Удалить, а с `with_board` — и связанную доску | `project_delete` | `portfolio_delete` | `goal_delete` (без `with_board`) |
| Добавить комментарий | `project_add_comment` | `portfolio_add_comment` | `goal_add_comment` |
| Изменить комментарий | `project_update_comment` | `portfolio_update_comment` | `goal_update_comment` |
| Удалить комментарий | `project_delete_comment` | `portfolio_delete_comment` | `goal_delete_comment` |
| Добавить пункт чек-листа | `project_add_checklist_item` | `portfolio_add_checklist_item` | - |
| Изменить один пункт, оставив непереданные поля как есть | `project_update_checklist_item` | `portfolio_update_checklist_item` | - |
| Переставить пункт перед другим | `project_move_checklist_item` | `portfolio_move_checklist_item` | - |
| Удалить один пункт | `project_delete_checklist_item` | `portfolio_delete_checklist_item` | - |
| Изменить несколько существующих пунктов по id | `project_update_checklist` | `portfolio_update_checklist` | - |
| Удалить весь чек-лист | `project_delete_checklist` | `portfolio_delete_checklist` | - |

- **Аргументы.** Чтение принимает `entity_id` и `fields`; инструменты `*_find` — `input`, `filter`, `order_by`, `order_asc`, `root_only`, `page`, `per_page`. Создание и изменение принимают `summary` (обязателен при создании), `description`, `lead`, `team_users`, `clients`, `followers`, `start` (у целей его нет), `end`, `tags`, `entity_status`, `parent_entity`, `team_access` и `links`, а изменение ещё `comment` и `version` (оптимистичная блокировка). Все инструменты принимают один и тот же селектор `fields` и возвращают сущность.
- **`links` только добавляются, а не заменяются**, и API их никогда не возвращает: прочитать или удалить существующую связь через этот сервер нельзя, а изменение, состоящее только из `links`, отклоняется — вместо того чтобы отчитаться об успехе, который Трекер молча проигнорировал.
- **Не входит в набор полей по умолчанию:** `checklistItems` (инструменты чек-листа возвращают сущность целиком, так что запрашивайте их, чтобы увидеть результат), `metricItems` и ключевые результаты цели `keyResultItems` — последние два доступны только на чтение. У целей свой набор значений `entityStatus` (`draft`, `according_to_plan`, `at_risk`, `blocked`, `achieved`, `partially_achieved`, `not_achieved`, `exceeded`, `cancelled`). Массовые изменения не поддерживаются.
EOF
python3 - <<PY
import pathlib
sp = pathlib.Path("$SP")
for readme, block, start, end in (("README.md","en_block.md",524,548),("README_ru.md","ru_block.md",521,545)):
    p = pathlib.Path(readme); lines = p.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)
    print(readme, "replacing:", repr(lines[start-1][:60]), "..", repr(lines[end-1][:60]))
    new = (sp/block).read_text()
    p.write_text("".join(lines[:start-1]) + new + "".join(lines[end:]))
PY
grep -n "" README.md | sed -n '516,528p' | cut -c1-90

# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

MCP Yandex Tracker is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides tools for interacting with Yandex Tracker API. It implements a FastMCP server with protocol-based architecture and optional Redis caching.

## Commands


For paginated methods, use `side_effect` for sequential returns: `mock.method.side_effect = [page1, []]`

## Adding New MCP Tools

### Implementation Checklist

1. **Protocol**: Add method signature to the matching `mcp_tracker/tracker/proto/*.py` (a new protocol also needs a `*ProtocolWrap` base, a `CacheCollection` slot, an `AppContext` field and wiring in `make_tracker_lifespan`)
2. **Client**: Implement in `mcp_tracker/tracker/custom/client.py`, through `self._request()` / `self._read()` - see *Talking to the Tracker API* above (this holds for read-only methods too)
3. **Caching**: Add wrapper in `mcp_tracker/tracker/caching/client.py`
4. **Tool**: Add function to appropriate module in `mcp_tracker/mcp/tools/`:
   - Queue read-only tools → `queue.py`
   - Queue write tools → `queue_write.py`
   - Global field/metadata tools → `field.py`
   - Issue/comment template tools → `template.py`
   - Board/sprint tools → `board.py`
   - Issue read-only tools → `issue_read.py`
   - Issue write tools → `issue_write.py`
   - User tools → `user.py`
   - Project read-only tools → `project.py`; write tools → `project_write.py`
   - Portfolio read-only tools → `portfolio.py`; write tools → `portfolio_write.py`
   - Goal read-only tools → `goal.py`; write tools → `goal_write.py`
5. **Tests**: Add to appropriate `tests/mcp/tools/test_*_tools.py`
6. **Docs**: Update `README.md`, `README_ru.md`, and `manifest.json`

### Tool Categories

| Category        | Module               | Read-Only |

**Entity tools** (project/portfolio/goal, read and write alike) are only registered when `settings.tracker_entities_enabled=True`.

### Test Requirements for New Tools

- Test success case with expected return data
- Test parameter passing (verify `call_args`)
- Test optional parameters (provided vs omitted)
- Test queue restrictions with `client_session_with_limits` if tool accesses issues/queues
- Add tool name to appropriate list in `tests/mcp/server/test_server_creation.py`:
  - Read-only tools → `READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES`
  - Write tools → `WRITE_TOOL_NAMES`
- For write tools, add test with `client_session_read_only` to verify not registered

## Configuration

Готово, `task` зелёный (1916 passed).

## Что появилось

**`rules/`** — пять коротких файлов на английском, AGENTS.md на них ссылается:

| Файл | О чём | Чем держится |
|---|---|---|
| `tool-naming.md` | `<entity>_<action>`, единственное число для одной записи, множественное для листинга; 5 старых `get_*` заморожены явным списком | `test_tool_conventions.py` |
| `tool-descriptions.md` | бюджет 1 предложение + 1 на ловушку, жёстко 40–350; что запрещено (внутренняя кухня, повтор схемы) и что обязательно (протухающий `version`, `summonees`, allow-list); общее — один раз в инструкциях сервера; параметр из 2+ тулов живёт в `params.py`; create/update симметричны | то же + `test_instructions.py` |
| `changelog.md` | секции, 1 буллет ≤2 строк, ≤3 подбуллета, `Internal` ≤2 буллета; диff от тега, а не по коммитам; старые версии не править | `test_release_metadata.py` |
| `docs.md` | формат таблицы по категориям, manifest — одно предложение <160, README_ru — перевод, а не суперсет; синхрон версий | `test_readme_coverage.py`, `test_release_metadata.py` |

**Три новых теста-сторожа.** Сервер собирается один раз на импорте, каждый тул — отдельный кейс: имя, длина описания, `readOnlyHint` против списков read/write, упоминание в обоих README, отсутствие в листингах несуществующих тулов, совпадение версий `pyproject`/`manifest`/`server.json` (включая тег OCI-образа) и наличие секции в CHANGELOG.

## Что пришлось починить, чтобы тесты были зелёными

- **6 описаний за потолком** сокращены: `boards_get_all` 665→301, `issue_get` 613→319, `issue_create` 597→318, `issue_update_checklist_item` 560→312, `issue_templates_get_all` 470→290, `queue_get_fields` 373→315. Ушла внутренняя кухня, остались ловушки и русские термины для поиска.
- **6 описаний ниже пола** (`goal_create` 33, `goal_delete` 29 и соседи) расширены до 90–150 — с русским термином и пометкой, что это сущность, а не очередь.
- **23 тула portfolio/goal вообще не упоминались ни в одном README** — были свёрнуты в «`portfolio_*`: те же инструменты». Секция проектов/портфелей/целей переписана в одну таблицу на все три типа (строка = что делает, столбцы = как называется) плюс 3 буллета под ней. Это же образец нового формата.

## Что осталось

Остальные категории README (очереди, задачи, доски, пользователи, шаблоны) всё ещё в старом формате «буллет + полный список Parameters», который дублирует JSON-схему — по новому `rules/docs.md` они должны стать таблицами. Это разовая переписка 64 КБ EN + 102 КБ RU, отдельным заходом: сказать — сделаю.

Коммитить не стал.

|---|---|

## Что выкинуто и почему это безопасно

Ушли построчные `Parameters:` — они дублировали JSON-схему. Проверил точечно то, что выглядело ценным: enum `relationship` у `issue_add_link` (9 значений) и пример `IssueWorkflow` у `issue_get_changelog` — оба лежат в схеме тула, клиент их видит. Ушли и внутренности вроде «делает параллельные запросы за двумя типами полей» и перечисление полей ответа.

Осталось всё, что нельзя увидеть в схеме, — собрано под таблицами максимум по 3 буллета на категорию:
- протухающий `version` и почему `issue_create` его не отдаёт годным;
- ссылочные поля одинаковы на create/update, `components`/`followers` заменяют список, `fields` перекрывает именованный аргумент, `null` очищает;
- переходы только из `issue_get_transitions`, перед `issue_close` — `type` + `issueTypesConfig`, elicitation у `issue_move`;
- доски не фильтруются `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` и почему поиск по `queue` неполон;
- шаблоны только на чтение, тело задачи в `fieldTemplates.description`;
- почему `hits`/`pages` иногда не приходят.

Пара мелких фактов переехала прямо в строку тула, где им место: `summonees` уведомляет, а `@login` в тексте — нет; `issue_move` меняет ключ задачи.

В CHANGELOG под Unreleased — одна запись в Documentation про `rules/` с тремя подбуллетами (по своим же правилам). Не коммитил.

# CHANGELOG

`CHANGELOG.md` is read by someone deciding whether to upgrade, and by an agent asked what
changed. Nothing else goes in it.

## Shape

- **Sections in this order**, omitted when empty: `### Features`, `### Bug Fixes`,
  `### Documentation`, `### Internal`.
- **One bullet per change, at most two lines.** Lead with the subject in bold; link the
  issue or PR.
- **At most three sub-bullets**, and only for something that changes what a caller does: a
  new argument, a changed default, a value no longer returned, a flag that gates the tool.
- **`### Internal`: at most two bullets per release.** For a change invisible from the
  outside that a contributor still needs to know (the `_request()` funnel, a dependency
  floor). A bullet that only lists what moved where does not belong - drop it.

## Content

- Say what changed for the caller, and - for a fix - what was wrong before.
- No library internals, no upstream PR archaeology, no rationale essays, no file or
  function names, no test names.
- Do not restate the tool description or the README. One line and the tool name is enough;
  the reader can look it up.

## Scope

Entries describe the diff since the previous tag (`git diff <last tag>..HEAD`), **not the
commits in between**. Something introduced and then reworked before the release is one
entry, in its final form; something that only exists on an unreleased branch is not an
entry at all. Getting this wrong once put a `with_board` argument in 0.8.0, for a tool that
did not ship until later.

## Versions

- Every release gets its own section, patch releases included.
- **Never edit a released section.**
- Unreleased work goes under `## [Unreleased]`, and becomes `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` at
  release time. `tests/test_release_metadata.py` fails if the version in `pyproject.toml`
  has no section.

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('rules/changelog.md')
p.write_text('''# CHANGELOG

`CHANGELOG.md` is read by someone deciding whether to upgrade, and by an agent asked what
changed. It says **what shipped**, not how it works. Nothing else goes in it.

## Shape

- **Sections in this order**, omitted when empty: `### Features`, `### Bug Fixes`,
  `### Documentation`, `### Internal`.
- **One bullet per change: the substance in one sentence, two at the most.** Lead with the
  subject in bold; link the issue or PR.
- **Sub-bullets are the exception, not the shape.** At most three, and only where a caller
  has to do something differently: a new argument, a changed default, a value no longer
  returned, a flag that gates the tool. Most changes need none and stay one line.
- **`### Internal`: at most two bullets per release.** For a change invisible from the
  outside that a contributor still needs to know (the `_request()` funnel, a dependency
  floor). A bullet that only lists what moved where does not belong - drop it.

## Content

- **Name what changed. Do not explain it.** The mechanics, the counts, the before/after
  detail and the reasoning belong in the commit message and in the code - a reader who
  wants them knows where to look.
- Do not restate the tool description, the README or the rule you just wrote. The name of
  the thing is enough to look it up.
- For a fix, one clause on what was wrong before is worth it. One clause.
- No library internals, no upstream PR archaeology, no file, function or test names.

## The size of an entry

Not this:

> - **`rules/`** - the conventions that kept being re-litigated per change (tool naming,
>   the description budget, CHANGELOG entries, README/manifest coverage), each with the
>   test that enforces it
>   - Six tool descriptions were over the 350-character budget and six under the
>     40-character floor; both ends are now checked, so a description can neither grow
>     into an essay nor be too thin to rank in tool search
>   - Both READMEs list the tools as one table per category - name, what it does, key
>     arguments - instead of restating the JSON schema argument by argument: the listing
>     went from 440 lines to 182

This:

> - **`rules/`** - guidelines for tool naming, tool and parameter descriptions and the
>   documentation, with the tests that enforce them

## Scope

Entries describe the diff since the previous tag (`git diff <last tag>..HEAD`), **not the
commits in between**. Something introduced and then reworked before the release is one
entry, in its final form; something that only exists on an unreleased branch is not an
entry at all. Getting this wrong once put a `with_board` argument in 0.8.0, for a tool that
did not ship until later.

## Versions

- Every release gets its own section, patch releases included.
- **Never edit a released section.**
- Unreleased work goes under `## [Unreleased]`, and becomes `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` at
  release time. `tests/test_release_metadata.py` fails if the version in `pyproject.toml`
  has no section.
''')
print("ok")
PY

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Features

- **Checklist write tools for issues** — checklists were read-only ([#44](https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/issues/44))

### Documentation

- **`rules/`** — guidelines for tool naming, tool and parameter descriptions and the documentation, with the tests that enforce them
- Both READMEs list the tools as one table per category instead of restating the JSON schema argument by argument

25	- An issue's **`boards`** is a typed field now. Tracker always returned it, but unmodelled: `extra="allow"` leaked it into answers while `outputSchema` never mentioned it and `fields` could not select it. The board id an issue names now feeds straight into the board tools

29	
30	- **The queue allow-lists match ignoring case.** `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` / `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES` were compared to the queue key exactly, and nothing upper-cased either side: Tracker's keys are upper-case, the variables are written by hand. 31	  - Both variables are normalised once on load into a set of upper-cased keys (`decode_queue_keys`), so a check is one hash lookup rather than a pass over the list per row; entries differing only in case collapse, and a list, set or tuple passed programmatically is normalised the same way
32	- With `TOOLS_CACHE_ENABLED=true`, the caller's raw OAuth/IAM token no longer ends up in the Redis cache key. aiocache builds keys by stringifying the cached method's arguments, so `YandexAuth`'s repr wrote the token verbatim into a namespace visible to `KEYS`/`SCAN`/`MONITOR`, RDB dumps and per-key metrics; secret fields now render as a SHA-256 fingerprint, which keeps entries distinct per caller and stops the token leaking into logs and tracebacks too
33	  - Cache entries written by earlier versions become misses and expire by TTL

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

message.content:
Another Claude session sent a message:
<teammate-message teammate_id="altitude" color="purple" summary="Altitude review findings on rules/ diff">
Verified all four questions by reading the actual files (AGENTS.md, rules/*.md, tests/mcp/server/test_tool_conventions.py, test_readme_coverage.py, test_server_creation.py, test_manifest.py, test_instructions.py, server.py, tools/__init__.py) and running the README-coverage regex against the real READMEs. Findings below, ordered by what's worth fixing.

## Worth fixing now

**1. `rules/README.md` and `AGENTS.md`'s new "## Rules" section duplicate the same index.**
- `AGENTS.md:5-14` and `rules/README.md` (whole file, 19 lines) both carry a table/list of the same four rule files with near-identical one-line descriptions ("what a tool is called", "CHANGELOG.md entries", etc.), plus near-identical closing sentences about what AGENTS.md still covers.
- Cost: exactly the drift the rules/ effort exists to prevent (docs.md even says "A fact present in only one of the two [READMEs] is a bug"). A fifth rule file added later has two indexes to update; missing one is invisible until someone notices.
- Right layer: pick one canonical index. AGENTS.md is the one agents read first and needs the "read this before touching X" trigger, so keep the short list there; make `rules/README.md` a one-paragraph pointer at AGENTS.md's Rules section instead of a second table, or vice versa.

**2. The README-coverage reverse check (`tests/mcp/server/test_readme_coverage.py`) is blind to the exact table shape `rules/docs.md` prescribes for tool families.**
- `LISTED_TOOL_PATTERN` only matches a tool name in the *first* cell of a table row (`^\| *\`name\` *\|`) or a bullet's own name. I ran it against the live READMEs: the Projects/Portfolios/Goals comparison table (README.md:494-511, mirrored in README_ru.md) puts the tool name in the *2nd/3rd/4th* column ("| One entity by id or shortId | `project_get` | `portfolio_get` | `goal_get` |"), so `listed_tools()` captures **zero** of the 21 project/portfolio/goal tool names from that table — confirmed by running the regex directly (`project_get`, `portfolio_get`, `goal_get`, etc. all return `False`).
- This is exactly the "family of identical tools ... shared explanation written once, above the table" shape `rules/docs.md` itself recommends and is the *only* listing of those 21 names in either README. The forward check (`test_every_tool_is_documented`) still passes them since it's a bare substring search, but the reverse check ("no listing names a tool that does not exist" - the one motivated by the `get_queue_metadata`/`queue_get_local_fields` phantom-tool incident) provides no protection at all for this table. A typo'd or stale entity tool name in this specific table would go undetected.
- This isn't a deliberate prose-exclusion tradeoff (unlike bullet/table anchoring in general, which is a reasonable choice - see below); it's a gap in the one non-first-column table format the rules explicitly endorse. Fix: extend the pattern to match any `\| *\`name\` *\|` cell, not just the line-leading one.

## Confirmed correct / not bandaids (no action needed)

**3. Test-file placement of `TOOL_NAME_ENTITIES`/`LEGACY_TOOL_NAMES` follows real precedent, not just similar-looking precedent.** `test_manifest.py` already imports `ENTITY_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES`/`ENTITY_WRITE_TOOL_NAMES` from `test_server_creation.py` (pre-existing, unrelated to this diff). The new pattern is actually an improvement on that precedent: `test_server_creation.py`'s lists are fully hand-maintained "expected" sets; `test_tool_conventions.py`'s `TOOL_IDS`/`TOOL_NAMES` are derived live from `create_mcp_server(...).list_tools()`, so only the *entity vocabulary* and *legacy exceptions* are hand-maintained, not the tool list itself. These constants aren't consumed by runtime code anywhere (`mcp_tracker/mcp/server.py`, `tools/__init__.py` - checked both, no references), so there's no case for promoting them into the package.

**4. Test is the right enforcement layer, not registration-time code.** Confirmed nothing in `server.py`/`tools/__init__.py` validates annotations or description length today - `test_tool_annotates_whether_it_writes` (pre-existing in `test_tool_conventions.py`'s neighborhood, same pattern) already treats `readOnlyHint` correctness as test-only. Measured all four points directly (repo builds clean, tests green: 452 in the new files, 1916+2skip full suite). Bottom line: nothing here is worth changing.

**1. Module-import-time cost, and does xdist multiply it**
`create_mcp_server()` alone: ~196ms. `asyncio.run(list_tools())` on top: 0.8ms — it's genuinely free, list_tools() does no I/O or lifespan work, just enumerates already-registered tool objects. So the "asyncio.run" framing overstates it; the real cost is server construction, same as any test touching a live server pays.

Tagged the module import with a pid-writing line and ran under the project's real config (`-n auto` is baked into `addopts` in pyproject.toml, not a flag I added) — confirmed it imports in all 12 worker processes (12 cores on this box), once each. That's ~2.4s of aggregate CPU, parallel across cores, not serialized into wall time.

Compared to the alternative: a session-scoped fixture would *also* build once per xdist worker (each worker gets its own session) — scoping doesn't change the count, only whether the cost lands at collection time or first-use. And it structurally can't be a fixture here anyway: the module list *is* the parametrize source for "one test case per tool," which is what makes a single bad description report as `test_tool_description_fits_the_budget[goal_create]` instead of a loop assertion. A function-scoped fixture (rebuild per case) would be the real waste: 89 tools × ~4 parametrized tests × 196ms ≈ 52s. The current form avoids exactly that. Not a cost worth naming.

**2. Real suite slowdown — measured, not estimated**
- Full suite minus the 3 new files: `1464 passed, 2 skipped in 14.42s` (wall 14.88s)
- Full suite with them: `1916 passed, 2 skipped in 16.26s` (wall 16.61s)
- Delta: ~1.8s wall, ~13% — real, but small in absolute terms, and it buys 452 test cases plus the release-metadata/README-coverage gate.
- The 3 files alone, single-process (`-n0`): 452 tests in 0.32s reported (0.87s wall, mostly Python/uv startup).
- Same 3 files alone under `-n auto`: 2.01s reported (2.57s wall) — the gap versus `-n0` (0.32s→2.01s) is 12-worker spawn/coordination overhead, which is inherent to the project's pre-existing `-n auto` default, not something this diff introduces.

**3. Repeated I/O or recomputation across parametrized cases: none found.**
- `READMES` dict built once at module level (both files together: 0.144ms to read 48KB+73KB).
- `REGISTERED_TOOLS`/`TOOL_IDS`/`TOOL_NAMES` built once in `test_tool_conventions.py`; `test_readme_coverage.py` *imports* them rather than recomputing — correct reuse.
- `LISTED_TOOL_PATTERN` compiled once, `listed_tools()` called only twice total (once per README), not per tool.
- The 178 `f"\`{tool_name}\`" in READMES[...]` substring checks (89 tools × 2 files): 0.57ms total for all of them.
- `test_server_creation.py`, imported for its name-list constants, has no expensive module-level work (plain list literals) — no double-build.
This is the efficient version of this test, not the naive one.

**4. Tool-description byte cost — quantified**
Computed exact UTF-8 byte deltas for all 12 touched descriptions:
- 6 over-budget ones trimmed: -364, -288, -273, -248, -168, -47 bytes
- 6 under-floor ones (goal/project/portfolio create/delete) expanded to clear the new 40-char floor: +109, +65, +116, +100, +100, +96 bytes
- **Net: -802 bytes across these 12 tools** (3485→2683 UTF-8 bytes) — the trims outweigh the expansions.
- Context: total description bytes across all 89 registered tools is ~12.9KB; input schemas alone are ~121KB. 802 bytes is ~6% of description payload and well under 1% of the full tool-listing response, sent once per session (not per call).
This change *reduces* the wire cost, not adds to it — not worth flagging as a regression, and too small to flag as a win either.

No proposed changes — everything measured as noise or as a net improvement.

<teammate-message teammate_id="simplify" color="green" summary="Simplification findings: tests, rules, tool descriptions">
Verified findings, grouped by your three buckets. Everything below was confirmed by reading the actual files (not the diff alone).

## 1. New test files

**A. `tests/mcp/server/test_tool_conventions.py:66`** — `READ_ONLY_NAMES = frozenset(READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES + ENTITY_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES)` re-derives a union that `tests/mcp/server/test_server_creation.py:117` already computes and names: `ALL_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES = READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES + ENTITY_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES`.
Cost: same 44-name union built twice under two names in two files; a reviewer has to notice both places agree.
Simpler: `from tests.mcp.server.test_server_creation import ALL_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` and `READ_ONLY_NAMES = frozenset(ALL_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES)` — drop the two-list import and the `+`.

**B. `tests/mcp/server/test_tool_conventions.py:68-71,74`** — `NAMED_BY_THE_RULE` / `NAMED_BY_THE_RULE_IDS` are a filtered copy of `REGISTERED_TOOLS`/`TOOL_IDS` that exist only to feed one `parametrize`, duplicating the shape already built two lines above for the other two tests in the file.
Simpler: parametrize `test_tool_is_named_entity_first` over `REGISTERED_TOOLS`/`TOOL_IDS` like its two siblings, and skip inside the body:
```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("tool", REGISTERED_TOOLS, ids=TOOL_IDS)
def test_tool_is_named_entity_first(tool: Tool) -> None:
    if tool.name in LEGACY_TOOL_NAMES:
        pytest.skip("legacy name, exempted by rules/tool-naming.md")
    ...
```
Drops 2 module constants, makes all 3 tests in the file share one parametrize shape.

**C. Cross-test-module imports** (your item 1, last bullet) — `test_readme_coverage.py:12` imports `TOOL_IDS, TOOL_NAMES` from `test_tool_conventions.py`, which in turn (`test_tool_conventions.py:17-20`) imports `READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES, ENTITY_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` from `test_server_creation.py`. Three test files chained together for shared constants; importing `test_readme_coverage.py` alone now also triggers `test_tool_conventions.py`'s module-level `asyncio.run(create_mcp_server(...))` server build as a side effect, and a rename of `TOOL_IDS`/`TOOL_NAMES` silently breaks a sibling test file.
Simpler: move `REGISTERED_TOOLS`/`TOOL_IDS`/`TOOL_NAMES` (and maybe `ALL_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES`) into `tests/mcp/server/conftest.py` (fixtures or plain module constants), and have both files import from there instead of from each other.

**D. `tests/mcp/server/test_readme_coverage.py:21-23`** — `LISTED_TOOL_PATTERN` matches two forms: a bullet `- **\`name\`**:` and a table cell `| \`name\` |`. But this same diff rewrote both READMEs into "one table per category" — I grepped both files for the bullet form and it matches **zero** times in either (`grep -cE '^- \*\*\`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\`\*\*' README.md README_ru.md` → 0/0), vs 50/50 table-row matches. The whole `(?:...|...)` alternation and the `match.groups()` / `if name` filtering in `listed_tools()` exist for a branch that never fires.
Simpler:
```python
LISTED_TOOL_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^\| *`([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)` *\|", re.MULTILINE)

def listed_tools(readme: str) -> set[str]:
    return {m.group(1) for m in LISTED_TOOL_PATTERN.finditer(readme)}
```

## 2. rules/*.md

**E. `rules/README.md` duplicates the "## Rules" section this diff adds to `AGENTS.md:49-58`.** Both are: an intro sentence on why `rules/` was split out, a list of the same 4 files, and a closing sentence on the AGENTS.md/rules boundary. Three of four one-line descriptions are word-for-word identical:
- `tool-descriptions.md`: "tool and parameter descriptions, and where a fact belongs" — identical in both
- `changelog.md`: "\`CHANGELOG.md\` entries" — identical in both
- `docs.md`: "\`README.md\`, \`README_ru.md\`, \`manifest.json\`, version sync" — identical in both

And the boundary statement is repeated: AGENTS.md says "This file covers the rest: architecture, the Tracker API's behaviour, and how to test." while rules/README.md says "AGENTS.md stays the place for architecture and for how the Tracker API behaves." — same fact, two files, will drift the next time a rule's scope changes.
Simpler: keep `rules/README.md` as the one canonical index (it's the natural GitHub landing page for the directory) and shrink the new AGENTS.md section to a single pointer:
```
## Rules

`rules/` holds conventions that are not negotiable per change, each with the test that
enforces it - see [rules/README.md](rules/README.md).
```
Cuts ~7 duplicated lines from AGENTS.md and removes the two-index drift risk.

**F. `rules/changelog.md:29-46` ("## The size of an entry") is disproportionate** — 18 of the file's 62 lines (~29%) are a "Not this / This" worked example that re-demonstrates rules already stated in prose immediately above, in "## Content" (lines 21-27: "Name what changed. Do not explain it." / "Do not restate the tool description, the README or the rule you just wrote."). The "Not this" block is itself a 3-level nested bullet essay — ironic, since the section exists to argue against exactly that shape. No other rules/*.md file spends this much space on one example (docs.md's worked example is 3 lines).
Simpler: cut "Not this" to 2-3 lines, or drop it and keep only the "This" line as one illustrative bullet under "## Content" rather than its own section.

## 3. Tool descriptions / README

Checked against the actual `Annotated` param aliases in `mcp_tracker/mcp/params.py` — several new descriptions restate what the shared param's own `Field(description=...)` already carries, which is exactly what `rules/tool-descriptions.md`'s own "Never in a description" list forbids ("Parameter names, types and defaults - the schema carries them, with their own text"):

**G. `project_delete`/`portfolio_delete`/`goal_delete`** (`project_write.py`, `portfolio_write.py`, `goal_write.py`) all take `entity_id: EntityID`, where `EntityID = Annotated[str, Field(description="Entity id or shortId")]` (`mcp_tracker/mcp/params.py:190-192`). Each new tool description adds "by its id or shortId" — near-verbatim restatement of that Field text. Simpler: drop that clause, e.g. `"Delete a Yandex Tracker project (in russian - 'проект'), optionally with its board. Cannot be undone."`

**H. `goal_create`/`portfolio_create`/`project_create`** each end with "Returns the created goal/portfolio/project." This is the obvious default for a create tool and directly contradicts the rule's own guidance one section up ("What comes back **instead of the obvious thing**"). Simpler: drop the trailing sentence entirely; nothing is lost since it's the default.

**I. `issue_get`** (`issue_read.py:46-47`) says "by a known key like 'QUEUE-123'" — but `issue_id: IssueID` where `IssueID = Annotated[str, Field(description="Issue ID in the format '<project>-<id>', like 'SOMEPROJECT-1'")]` (`params.py:66-68`) already carries a format example (different placeholder string, same fact). The README table then adds a *third* restatement: the "Issue Operations" table's Key arguments column has `` issue_id (`"QUEUE-123"`) ``. Note `rules/docs.md`'s own justifying example for when a README may spell out a format ("Spell an argument out only where the schema cannot: a format like \`QUEUE-123\`") is literally this case — except the schema *can* and does carry it already, so the rule's own stated exception doesn't actually hold here. Simpler: drop "like 'QUEUE-123'" from the tool description (just "by a known key"), and drop the `("QUEUE-123")` aside from the README row - `issue_id` alone is enough, consistent with how every other row in that table lists bare argument names.

Nothing above touches correctness - only added complexity/duplication. Happy to also check the remaining tool descriptions against their param schemas if useful, but G/H/I already cover the clearest, verified cases.
</teammate-message>

`rules/tool-descriptions.md`.

Both rules come from real damage. Descriptions grew into essays a client pays for in
context on every call, and were cut back by hand twice; `issue_get` and `get_priorities`
went the other way and could not be found by tool search at all.
"""

import re

import pytest
from mcp.types import Tool

from tests.mcp.server.test_server_creation import ALL_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES
from tests.mcp.server.tool_listing import REGISTERED_TOOLS, TOOL_NAMES

# Entity prefixes a tool name may start with. A tool for a new entity means adding
# its prefix here, in the same PR - a deliberate line, not a regex that lets
# anything through.
TOOL_NAME_ENTITIES = frozenset(
    {
        "board",
        "boards",
        "comment",
        "goal",
        "issue",
        "issues",
        "portfolio",
        "project",
        "queue",
        "queues",
        "user",
        "users",
    }
)

# Named before the rule existed. A tool name is API - clients call it by name - so
# these stay as they are, and nothing new is named this way.
LEGACY_TOOL_NAMES = frozenset(
    {
        "get_global_fields",
        "get_issue_types",
        "get_priorities",
        "get_resolutions",
        "get_statuses",
    }
)

MIN_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH = 40
MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH = 350

TOOL_NAME_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^([a-z]+)(?:_[a-z0-9]+)+$")

READ_ONLY_NAMES = frozenset(ALL_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES)
NAMED_BY_THE_RULE = [
    tool for tool in REGISTERED_TOOLS if tool.name not in LEGACY_TOOL_NAMES
]


def tool_id(tool: Tool) -> str:
    return tool.name


@pytest.mark.parametrize("tool", NAMED_BY_THE_RULE, ids=tool_id)
def test_tool_is_named_entity_first(tool: Tool) -> None:
    match = TOOL_NAME_PATTERN.match(tool.name)
    assert match is not None, (
        f"'{tool.name}' is not <entity>_<action> - see rules/tool-naming.md"
    )
    assert match.group(1) in TOOL_NAME_ENTITIES, (
        f"'{tool.name}' starts with '{match.group(1)}', which is not a known entity. "
        "Name it after the entity it acts on, or add the entity to TOOL_NAME_ENTITIES."
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", sorted(LEGACY_TOOL_NAMES))
def test_legacy_names_are_still_registered(name: str) -> None:
    """The exception list may not outlive the tools it excuses."""
    assert name in TOOL_NAMES, (
        f"'{name}' is no longer registered - drop it from LEGACY_TOOL_NAMES"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("tool", REGISTERED_TOOLS, ids=tool_id)
def test_tool_description_fits_the_budget(tool: Tool) -> None:
    description = tool.description or ""

    assert len(description) >= MIN_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH, (
        f"'{tool.name}' has {len(description)} characters of description. Too thin to "
        "rank in tool search - say what it does and what comes back."
    )
    assert len(description) <= MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH, (
        f"'{tool.name}' has {len(description)} characters of description, over the "
        f"{MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH} budget. What a caller acts on stays; the rest goes "
        "to README.md - see rules/tool-descriptions.md."
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("tool", REGISTERED_TOOLS, ids=tool_id)
def test_tool_annotates_whether_it_writes(tool: Tool) -> None:
    assert tool.annotations is not None, f"'{tool.name}' declares no ToolAnnotations"
    assert tool.annotations.readOnlyHint is (tool.name in READ_ONLY_NAMES), (
        f"'{tool.name}' has readOnlyHint={tool.annotations.readOnlyHint}, which "
        "contradicts the read-only/write lists in test_server_creation.py"
    )

**Дыра в обратной проверке README** (altitude нашёл, я перепроверил)
Регекс ловил имя только в первой ячейке строки, поэтому таблица «проекты/портфели/цели», где имена во 2–4 колонках, была невидима: проверялось **50 тулов из 89**. Заменил регекс на разбор ячеек: строка, начинающаяся с имени, даёт имя из первой ячейки; строка, начинающаяся с прозы (таблица семейств), — все ячейки-имена. Теперь **89/89 в обоих README**, `queue_id` и прочие аргументы не считаются тулами, фантом вроде `get_queue_metadata` ловится. Заодно ушла мёртвая ветка под старый bullet-формат (после перевода на таблицы она не срабатывала ни разу), а `LISTED` считается один раз на модуль, а не в каждом из 178 кейсов. Прямая проверка тоже усилена: тул должен иметь строку в таблице, а не просто где-то упоминаться.

**Правила дублировали AGENTS.md**
- Индекс правил был в двух местах слово в слово. Канонический — `rules/README.md`, в AGENTS.md остался один абзац-указатель.
- `rules/tool-naming.md` пересказывал гейт `TRACKER_READ_ONLY` — убрано, там уже есть ссылка на таблицу в AGENTS.md.
- `rules/tool-descriptions.md` заново выводил пример «создал скаляром — обновить не смог», который дословно есть в AGENTS.md — теперь ссылка.
- В `rules/changelog.md` блок «Not this» ужат вдвое: он сам был трёхуровневым эссе против трёхуровневых эссе.

**Описания нарушали собственное правило** — три `*_delete` пересказывали текст `EntityID` («by its id or shortId»), три `*_create` заканчивались очевидным «Returns the created X», `issue_get` дублировал формат из `IssueID`. Всё убрано, все остались выше пола в 40 символов (минимум теперь 69). В README-таблице убрана та же приписка `("QUEUE-123")`, а сноска у `goal_delete` вынесена из ячейки с именем — чтобы правило разбора оставалось простым.

## Не менял

- **Efficiency не нашёл ничего**: сборка сервера на импорте ~196 мс на xdist-воркера (session-фикстура стоила бы столько же, function-scoped — ~52 с), суите +1.8 с за 452 кейса, описания стали на 802 байта легче.
- **`ROOT` считается в трёх файлах** с разным `parents[N]` — они лежат на разной глубине, так что это одно и то же выражение относительно разных точек, а общая константа потребовала бы либо импорта из conftest, либо модуля, чей импорт тянет сборку сервера туда, где она не нужна.
- Совет заменить фильтрованный список на `pytest.skip` для legacy-имён — тогда в выводе появляется 5 пропущенных тестов на ровном месте.
